description: Synthesis-oriented filters for chemical space estimation (strict v2)
sources: Bruns & Watson, J. Med. Chem. 2012, 55, 9763 — Lilly MedChem Rules (reactivity/instability subset)
IanAWatson/Lilly-Medchem-Rules GitHub — queries/reject1 (80 rejection queries, custom QRY format)
Hartenfeller et al., J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2011, 51, 3093 — 58 HTE reactions
Grygorenko et al., iScience 2020, 23(11), 101681 — Enamine REAL methodology
Roughley & Jordan, J. Med. Chem. 2011, 54, 3451 — Medicinal chemistry reaction survey
Clayden, Greeves, Warren — Organic Chemistry, 2nd ed. — FG incompatibility textbook

lilly_instability_smarts.name: aldehyde
lilly_instability_smarts.reason: Reactive electrophile, forms Schiff bases with amines in vivo and during purification

lilly_instability_smarts.name: hemiacetal
lilly_instability_smarts.reason: Latent aldehyde, hydrolyzes under mild conditions

lilly_instability_smarts.name: thiol_free
lilly_instability_smarts.reason: Oxidation-prone, dimerizes to disulfide on standing

lilly_instability_smarts.name: disulfide
lilly_instability_smarts.reason: Redox-labile bond, cleaves under mild reducing conditions

lilly_instability_smarts.name: activated_ester
lilly_instability_smarts.reason: Activated esters react with amines during handling

lilly_instability_smarts.name: alkyl_iodide
lilly_instability_smarts.reason: Strong alkylating agent, reacts with nucleophiles

lilly_instability_smarts.name: thiomethyl_ketone
lilly_instability_smarts.reason: Thioether alpha to carbonyl, prone to elimination

pd_catalyzed_i.description: Pd-catalyzed coupling at Iodide (highest reactivity). No halogen priority exclusions.

exclusions_on_any_bb.reason: Pd catalyst poisoning by free thiol (Roughley & Jordan 2011)
Azo groups poison Pd catalyst
Free phosphine competes with ligand for Pd coordination
Bifunctional ArBr/ArI + ArB(OH)2 self-polymerizes
Ambiguous regioselectivity: two or more aromatic iodides on same molecule
Ambiguous regioselectivity: two or more aromatic bromides on same molecule
Ambiguous regioselectivity: two or more aromatic chlorides on same molecule

pd_catalyzed_br.description: Pd-catalyzed coupling at Bromide. Blocked if Iodide is present.

exclusions_on_any_bb.reason: Pd catalyst poisoning by free thiol
Bifunctional ArBr/ArI + ArB(OH)2 self-polymerizes
Ambiguous regioselectivity: two or more aromatic iodides on same molecule
Ambiguous regioselectivity: two or more aromatic bromides on same molecule
Ambiguous regioselectivity: two or more aromatic chlorides on same molecule

exclusions_on_halide_bb.reason: Selective Reactivity: Pd-coupling priority I > Br. Iodide must be reacted first.

pd_catalyzed_cl.description: Pd-catalyzed coupling at Chloride. Blocked if Bromide or Iodide is present.

exclusions_on_any_bb.reason: Pd catalyst poisoning by free thiol
Bifunctional ArBr/ArI + ArB(OH)2 self-polymerizes
Ambiguous regioselectivity: two or more aromatic iodides on same molecule
Ambiguous regioselectivity: two or more aromatic bromides on same molecule
Ambiguous regioselectivity: two or more aromatic chlorides on same molecule

exclusions_on_halide_bb.reason: Selective Reactivity: Pd-coupling priority I > Br > Cl. Bromide or Iodide must be reacted first.

amide_coupling.description: COOH activation (Schotten-Baumann, sulfonamide) produces electrophilic intermediates that react with competing nucleophiles

exclusions_on_acid_bb.reason: Aldehyde on acid BB competes for amine via imine formation
Free amine on acid BB causes self-acylation / oligomerization

exclusions_on_amine_bb.reason: Primary alcohol on amine BB causes competing ester formation
Free thiol on amine BB reacts faster than amine with acyl chloride
Aldehyde on amine BB causes imine formation with amine BB itself

reductive_amination.description: NaBH3CN / NaBH(OAc)3 reduces imines but also reduces other carbonyls non-selectively

exclusions_on_any_bb.reason: Isocyanate reacts with amine before imine formation
Acyl halide reacts with amine before aldehyde
Epoxide ring-opens under reductive amination conditions

exclusions_on_amine_bb.reason: Extra aldehyde on amine BB causes self-reductive amination

base_sensitive.description: Strong base conditions (Wittig ylide formation, Grignard organometallic) are incompatible with acidic protons and strained electrophiles

exclusions_on_any_bb.reason: beta-lactone ring-opening under basic/organometallic conditions
beta-lactam ring-opening under basic/organometallic conditions
Acidic proton quenches Grignard/Wittig reagent (Clayden ch.10)
Primary aliphatic amine proton quenches Grignard reagent
Thiol proton quenches Grignard reagent
Aldehyde reacts with Grignard before intended electrophile (Clayden ch.10)
Isocyanate reacts with Grignard reagent

click_chemistry.description: CuAAC and RuAAC click reactions are sensitive to competing coordination and reduction

exclusions_on_any_bb.reason: Thiol coordinates Cu(I) catalyst, reduces efficacy
Phosphine reduces Cu(I) to inactive Cu(0)

williamson_ether.description: Williamson ether synthesis uses strong base (NaH, KOH) to generate alkoxide

exclusions_on_any_bb.reason: Aldehyde competes via Cannizzaro or aldol reaction under base
Carboxylic acid neutralizes base, prevents alkoxide formation
Aliphatic amine competes as nucleophile in SN2

mitsunobu.description: Mitsunobu reactions use DIAD/DEAD + PPh3, sensitive to multiple acidic NH/OH groups

exclusions_on_any_bb.reason: Carboxylic acid competes as second nucleophile under Mitsunobu
Thiol competes as nucleophile under Mitsunobu conditions

steric_hindrance.description: Both reactants having severely hindered reactive sites drastically reduces yield. Reject pair only when BOTH reactants match a hindrance pattern.

patterns.name: ortho_disubstituted_aryl_halide
patterns.reason: ortho,ortho-disubstituted aryl halide, very poor cross-coupling yield (Roughley & Jordan 2011)
patterns.note: Suzuki/BH coupling of 2,6-disubstituted aryl halides typically <20% yield

patterns.name: neopentyl_carbon
patterns.reason: Quaternary carbon adjacent to reactive site, extreme steric shielding

patterns.name: tert_butyl_adjacent_to_reactive
patterns.reason: tert-butyl group creates significant steric bulk near coupling site

patterns.name: ortho_disubstituted_boronic_acid
patterns.reason: ortho,ortho-disubstituted boronic acid, poor transmetalation in Suzuki (Barder et al.)
